doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Visiting Sun Ra's house and John Gilmore
summary: He describes visiting Sun Ra's home, being greeted by name, the artwork, and the devoted John Gilmore living there.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever get a sense of what it was like at Sun Ra’s home and place of rehearsal? Did any of his members ever describe that to you?

Well I used to go and visit there, Monk. I used to visit the place. This is as thrilling as it gets. When I went to Sun Ra’s and the first time I went and he said, “Hello, Jerry.” That was it. I had arrived. He knew my name. And he was talking to, I remember very clearly he was talking to an Italian video producer, you know, from Italy, who was trying to © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

make a deal with Sun Ra for some kind of video or something. I guess Sun Ra wanted to get off the phone with him and he said, “I’m talking to Jerry. I have to go.” That was thrilling to me. So I have wonderful memories of visiting Sun Ra’s place and, you know, meeting some of the band there. And there was crazy artwork there, artwork that listeners had sent him or that followers of the band, friends, whatever, had sent him. And the place was what Sun Ra’s place you might expect it to look like. It was very cool. John Gilmore lived in the same house as Sun Ra. And John Gilmore was very sweet and soft spoken and no one was, you know from history that no one was more devoted to Sun Ra and his music than John Gilmore, recording very few albums away from the Arkestra. So he was very sweet. He lived there. And there were other members of the Arkestra coming through. I didn’t know who lived there and who didn’t. I didn’t know what was going on. I was just thrilled to be there.
